name: LangChain
desc: Open-source Python and JavaScript framework for building LLM-powered applications and agents. Provides composable abstractions for chains, tools, memory, and retrieval to streamline AI application development.
notes:
Core framework is MIT-licensed and free. LangSmith (observability) and LangGraph Cloud (managed orchestration) are separate commercial products from LangChain Inc. LangGraph (graph-based agent orchestration) is a distinct but closely related project cataloged separately.

---

name: LlamaIndex
desc: Open-source data framework for building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) applications. Provides data ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and query engines for connecting LLMs to external documents and data sources.
notes:
Core framework is MIT-licensed. LlamaCloud is a commercial managed service for production RAG pipelines offered by LlamaIndex (formerly Jerry Liu's company). Formerly known as GPT Index before rebranding to LlamaIndex.

---

name: Qdrant
desc: High-performance vector database and similarity search engine built in Rust for storing, indexing, and querying vector embeddings. Designed for semantic search, RAG, and AI application backends with filtering support.
notes:
Core engine is Apache 2.0 licensed and freely self-hostable. Qdrant Cloud is a managed, fully-hosted offering with a free tier (1GB cluster). Supports sparse vectors, payload filtering, and multi-tenancy. Written in Rust for performance and memory safety.

---

name: Ollama
desc: Open-source runtime for running large language models locally on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API, supports NVIDIA/AMD GPU acceleration, and manages model downloads via a curated library.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Supports CUDA (NVIDIA), ROCm (AMD), and Metal (Apple Silicon) acceleration. Modelfile system enables custom model configuration. Provides a Docker image for server deployments. Works with Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, and many other open-weight model families.

---

name: vLLM
desc: High-throughput LLM inference and serving engine using PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory management. Provides OpenAI-compatible APIs, continuous batching, and support for distributed multi-GPU inference.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Key innovation is PagedAttention — a memory management technique enabling 24x higher throughput vs naive implementations. Supports tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism for multi-GPU deployments. Widely used in production LLM serving.

---

name: Hugging Face Hub
desc: Central platform for hosting, discovering, and sharing AI models, datasets, and Spaces. Provides Git-based model versioning, model cards, inference APIs, and a collaborative ecosystem for the ML community.
notes:
Core public model/dataset hosting is free. Pro plan (\$9/month) adds storage and compute credits. Enterprise plan starts at \$50/user/month with SSO, audit logs, and private regions. A self-hosted Enterprise Hub version exists but is distinct from the public platform.

---

name: Pinecone
desc: Fully managed serverless vector database for semantic search, recommendation systems, and RAG applications. Provides automatic scaling, filtered search, and multi-tenancy with pay-per-use billing for reads, writes, and storage.
notes:
Fully managed cloud service only — no self-hosting option. Free Starter plan includes 2GB storage and limited usage. Standard production plans have a usage-based pricing model with read units, write units, and storage metering. Transitioned to serverless architecture in 2024.

---

name: Weaviate
desc: Open-source vector database with native multi-modal support, hybrid search (dense + sparse), and built-in ML model integrations. Supports semantic search, question answering, and classification at scale.
notes:
Core engine is BSD-3-Clause licensed (open-source). Weaviate Cloud (WCD) is a managed service with a free sandbox tier. Supports GraphQL and REST APIs. Includes built-in vectorizer modules for OpenAI, Cohere, HuggingFace embeddings.

---

name: LangGraph
desc: Graph-based orchestration framework for building stateful multi-step AI agents with fine-grained control over loops, branching, and persistence. Designed for reliable, controllable agentic application workflows.
notes:
Developed and maintained by LangChain Inc. MIT-licensed open-source library. LangGraph Cloud is a separate commercial managed deployment product. Distinct from LangChain (cataloged separately) — LangGraph focuses on stateful, cyclical workflows for agents.

---

name: CrewAI
desc: Open-source Python framework for orchestrating autonomous AI agent teams. Enables role-based agent design, task delegation, memory sharing, and tool integration for complex multi-agent collaborative workflows.
notes:
Core Python framework is MIT-licensed. CrewAI Enterprise offers managed cloud deployment at custom pricing. Free plan on CrewAI cloud includes ~50 executions/month. Integrates with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent-to-Agent) communication protocols.

---

name: Langfuse
desc: Open-source LLM observability and tracing platform for debugging, monitoring, and evaluating LLM applications. Provides trace visualization, prompt management, evaluation workflows, and cost analytics.
notes:
Core platform is MIT-licensed and self-hostable (via Docker). Langfuse Cloud offers a free Hobby tier (50K traces/month, 30-day retention). Core plan at \$29/month, Pro at \$199/month. Enterprise self-hosted plans available with SSO and advanced RBAC.

---

name: OpenAI API Platform
desc: OpenAI's developer API platform providing programmatic access to GPT-4o, o1, Whisper, DALL·E, Embeddings, and Assistants API. Enables integration of OpenAI models into third-party applications and workflows.
notes:
Distinct from the ChatGPT consumer product (tool:chatgpt) and from individual OpenAI models. Pricing is purely usage-based (per-token and per-request). Provides API access to all current OpenAI models including reasoning (o-series), GPT-4o, vision, TTS, ASR, embeddings, and image generation.

---

name: Anthropic API
desc: Anthropic's developer API providing access to Claude model family for text generation, vision, tool use, and document analysis. Offers usage-based token pricing and safety-focused model behavior.
notes:
Distinct from Claude consumer product (tool:claude) and individual Claude model records. API access requires signup and payment method. Supports Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Claude 3 Opus. Available on AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI as third-party integrations.

---

name: llama.cpp
desc: C/C++ inference framework for running large language models locally using GGUF quantized model formats. Supports CPU-only inference with optional GPU acceleration on CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, and ROCm backends.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Originally created by Georgi Gerganov; repository moved to ggml-org organization. The GGUF model format originated from this project. Foundation for many local LLM tools including Ollama. Supports LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, and many other architectures.

---

name: Chroma
desc: Open-source embedding database for AI applications. Provides a developer-friendly API for storing, querying, and managing embeddings locally or in a client-server deployment, with native Python and JavaScript clients.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Designed primarily for prototyping and local-first development. Chroma Cloud (managed service) is in development. Popular choice for RAG prototyping due to its simple in-memory and persistent local modes. Distinct from Pinecone and Weaviate in its local-first, developer-friendly philosophy.

---

name: AutoGen
desc: Microsoft Research's open-source framework for building event-driven, distributed multi-agent AI systems. Supports asynchronous messaging, agent teams, human-in-the-loop workflows, and cross-language agent communication.
notes:
MIT-licensed. AutoGen 0.4 (released 2024) introduced a redesigned asynchronous, event-driven architecture. Supports Python and .NET agents. AutoGen Studio is a no-code UI companion. Distinct from LangGraph and CrewAI in its emphasis on distributed, asynchronous agent communication patterns.

---

name: Replicate
desc: Cloud platform for running AI models via API with pay-per-use pricing. Hosts thousands of open-source and official AI models for image generation, video, language, and audio tasks without infrastructure management.
notes:
Pure usage-based pricing — no free tier beyond an initial credit allowance. Billing by hardware-seconds (for community models) or by output units (for official models). Cog is Replicate's open-source tool for packaging custom models. Supports private model deployment with autoscaling.

---

name: Model Context Protocol SDK
subtype: Open Agent Protocol Specification and SDK
desc: Open standard and software development kit introduced by Anthropic that standardizes how AI applications and agents securely access external context, enterprise databases, file systems, and API tools over JSON-RPC.
notes:
MIT-licensed open standard. Eliminates custom point-to-point integrations by providing reusable server and client abstractions implemented across Python, TypeScript, and Kotlin.

---

name: LiteLLM
desc: Open-source AI proxy and gateway that unifies calls to 100+ LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Ollama) using the standard OpenAI input-output format, handling load balancing, fallbacks, and cost tracking.
notes:
Core proxy is MIT-licensed. LiteLLM Enterprise offers dedicated virtual key management, SSO, rate limits, and custom billing dashboards for production deployments.

---

name: SGLang
subtype: Fast Serving Engine & Structured Decoding Framework
desc: High-throughput serving engine and programming language for large language models. Optimizes complex prompt workflows, multi-turn chat loops, and constrained JSON decodings with RadixAttention KV-cache reuse.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by researchers from LMSYS and UC Berkeley. RadixAttention retains KV-caches across multiple API calls, significantly speeding up complex reasoning and agent workflows.

---

name: TensorRT-LLM
desc: Open-source Python and C++ inference optimization library engineered by NVIDIA. Compiles and executes large language models with kernel fusions, in-flight batching, FP8 quantization, and multi-GPU tensor parallelism.
notes:
Released under the Apache 2.0 license. Powers NVIDIA NIM microservices. Maximizes token throughput and minimizes first-token latency on NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell hardware architectures.

---

name: Unsloth
desc: High-speed, memory-efficient fine-tuning library for open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma). Uses custom hand-written GPU Triton kernels to speed up LoRA and QLoRA training by up to 5x while reducing VRAM usage by 80%.
notes:
Core software open-source under Apache 2.0. Unsloth Pro and Enterprise provide multi-GPU distributed fine-tuning and commercial support. Enables fine-tuning large 70B parameter models on modest GPU configurations.

---

name: Axolotl
desc: Config-driven tool designed to streamline the post-training and fine-tuning of foundation language models. Supports full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, and PPO via simple YAML configurations across multi-GPU setups.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Supports FlashAttention, xFormers, DeepSpeed, and FSDP natively. Serves as a standard training harness for open-source AI researchers and community model builders.

---

name: DSPy
desc: Stanford University's open-source framework for programmatically optimizing language model prompts and weights. Replaces brittle hand-written prompt templates with modular Python signatures that are compiled and auto-tuned algorithmically.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Treats LLM pipelines as parameterized programs with automated optimizers (Teleprompters / MIPRO) that systematically discover high-performing few-shot demonstrations and prompt variations.

---

name: OpenRouter
desc: Unified API gateway that aggregates hundreds of proprietary and open-weight AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible interface, offering automated fallback routing, competitive per-token pricing, and transparent latency benchmarks.
notes:
Purely usage-based without subscriptions; charges exact upstream provider costs plus minimal transaction margins. Supports crypto and fiat credit top-ups. Includes a free tier for select open-source models.

---

name: Together AI
desc: High-performance cloud platform providing fast API inference for open-source AI models, dedicated GPU compute clusters, and custom model fine-tuning environments with enterprise SOC 2 compliance.
notes:
Billed on per-token consumption for serverless endpoints and per-hour rates for dedicated H100 GPU clusters. Known for high token-per-second inference speeds powered by custom flash-attention kernels.

---

name: Groq Cloud
desc: Ultra-fast AI inference platform powered by custom Language Processing Unit (LPU) semiconductor hardware. Serves open-weight LLMs, vision, and Whisper transcription models at hundreds of tokens per second with near-instant response times.
notes:
Provides a free tier with daily rate limits. Paid Pay-As-You-Go tier charges standard per-million-token consumption. LPU deterministic architecture avoids typical GPU queuing jitter, enabling real-time conversational voice agents.

---

name: Modal
subtype: Serverless Cloud Compute Platform for AI
desc: Serverless cloud infrastructure platform that allows developers to run Python code, containerized AI workloads, batch model inference, and fine-tuning jobs on cloud GPUs with sub-second cold starts and per-second billing.
notes:
Includes $30/month in free compute credits for all users. Billed strictly by execution seconds across CPU, memory, and GPU (T4, A10G, L4, A100, H100) allocations. Container environments are defined directly in native Python code.

---

name: RunPod
subtype: Distributed Cloud GPU & Serverless AI Platform
desc: Cloud computing provider specializing in affordable GPU rental pods, distributed training clusters, and serverless AI worker endpoints for deploying inference APIs, image generators, and machine learning models globally.
notes:
Offers Secure Cloud (Tier 3/4 data centers) and Community Cloud (budget pricing). Billed by the minute/second. Serverless GPU endpoints automatically scale to zero when idle to save infrastructure costs.

---

name: Braintrust
desc: Enterprise evaluation, tracing, and prompt-engineering platform for LLM applications. Provides CI/CD regression testing, dataset curation, automated scoring, real-time production monitoring, and prompt playground environments.
notes:
Free plan includes unlimited seats and a monthly allotment of evaluation records and traces. Pro plan ($50/month) and Enterprise plans offer custom retention, SSO, private cloud deployments, and dedicated support.

---

name: Arize Phoenix
desc: Open-source AI observability library and dashboard for tracing LLM execution steps, evaluating RAG retrieval pipelines, troubleshooting hallucination rates, and benchmarking agent execution graphs using OpenTelemetry standards.
notes:
Released under Apache 2.0 license. Can be run entirely locally inside a Jupyter notebook or Docker container without transmitting telemetry to third-party clouds. Arize Cloud provides managed SaaS hosting.

---

name: Guardrails AI
desc: Open-source Python and JavaScript framework that enforces structural guarantees, type safety, PII redaction, toxicity filtering, and prompt injection defense on LLM inputs and outputs using community-authored validators.
notes:
Core framework is Apache 2.0 licensed. Operates Guardrails Hub, a marketplace of pre-built validators (regex matching, hallucination detection, schema compliance). Guardrails Server provides a containerized microservice API.

---

name: pgvector
subtype: Vector Similarity Search Extension for PostgreSQL
desc: Open-source vector similarity search extension for PostgreSQL. Stores exact and approximate nearest-neighbor vector embeddings alongside relational relational records using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing methods.
notes:
Distributed under the PostgreSQL License. Widely deployed across AWS RDS, Supabase, Neon, Azure PostgreSQL, and self-hosted database clusters to consolidate vectors and transactional data in a single ACID engine.

---

name: LanceDB
desc: Developer-friendly, serverless open-source vector database built on the columnar Lance data format. Supports disk-native vector search, multi-modal storage, hybrid retrieval, and zero-infrastructure local embedding storage.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Can run serverlessly in-process (like DuckDB or SQLite) embedded directly in Python/Node applications, querying disk and object storage (S3/GCS) without dedicated database servers. LanceDB Cloud offers enterprise managed hosting.

name: Milvus
desc: Open-source cloud-native distributed vector database designed to manage and search tens of billions of vector embeddings in milliseconds. Built with decoupled storage and compute for massive enterprise scale.

Graduated LF AI & Data Foundation project under Apache 2.0. Zilliz Cloud provides the fully managed enterprise cloud edition. Supports HNSW, IVF, and GPU-accelerated indexes (Knowhere).

---

name: Faiss
desc: Open-source C++ and Python library developed by Meta Fundamental AI Research for efficient dense vector clustering and similarity search across billion-scale datasets with complete GPU acceleration and quantization support.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Foundational low-level algorithm library underlying many production vector databases and retrieval systems. Features Product Quantization (PQ) and Inverted File (IVF) indexes.

---

name: Haystack
desc: Production-ready open-source Python framework from deepset for constructing customizable RAG pipelines, semantic search engines, and agent workflows using a typed, directed acyclic graph (DAG) component architecture.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Haystack 2.0 features modular component connections, flexible document store adapters, and seamless integration with deepset Cloud for enterprise deployments.

---

name: txtai
desc: Open-source all-in-one embeddings database that combines vector indexing, relational SQL storage, document extraction, and graph networks to power semantic search, knowledge graphs, and LLM orchestration.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by NeuML. Enables querying multimodal data and knowledge graphs using standard SQL syntax combined with vector similarity matching.

---

name: RAGFlow
desc: Open-source RAG engine based on deep document understanding. Extracts and parses unstructured data from complex multi-column PDFs, financial tables, slides, and scanned forms with vision-based document layout analysis.
notes:
Apache 2.0 licensed by InfiniFlow. Solves the "garbage in, garbage out" challenge in RAG by visualizing document chunks and preserving tabular structure across multi-page corporate PDFs.

---

name: Microsoft GraphRAG
desc: Modular RAG pipeline developed by Microsoft Research that extracts structured knowledge graphs and entity communities from unstructured text documents, enabling holistic global summarization over entire private corpuses.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Addresses standard vector RAG's failure to answer query-focused global questions (e.g., "What are the major themes across all 50 reports?") by leveraging hierarchical Leiden community detection.

---

name: Dify
desc: Open-source platform combining Backend-as-a-Service and visual workflow orchestration for AI applications. Enables teams to visually build multi-agent systems, complex RAG pipelines, and API integrations with one-click deployment.
notes:
Open-source under Apache 2.0 with commercial restrictions in the Dify Open Source License. Easily deployed via Docker Compose. Dify Cloud provides a managed SaaS offering with free sandbox credits.

---

name: Flowise
desc: Open-source drag-and-drop UI tool built on LangChain.js that enables developers to visually configure LLM chains, conversational agents, custom tool integrations, memory nodes, and vector database embeddings.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Built using Node.js and React. Deploys as an independent container or npm package, exposing finished flows as embeddable chat widgets or REST API endpoints.

---

name: Langflow
subtype: Visual Framework for Multi-Agent & RAG Systems
desc: Visual, Python-based web UI framework designed for prototyping and testing multi-agent workflows, custom prompt chains, and RAG architectures with live execution tracing and reusable component building blocks.
notes:
Acquired by DataStax. MIT-licensed. Every visual block corresponds directly to Python code that developers can inspect, customize, and export into production applications.

---

name: n8n
subtype: Self-Hostable Workflow Automation with AI Agents
desc: Fair-code workflow automation platform that integrates 400+ business applications with native LangChain AI nodes, enabling developers to build autonomous AI agents, chat triggers, and custom data sync pipelines.
notes:
Source-available under Sustainable Use License (free for self-hosted internal business use). n8n Cloud offers managed tiers. AI Agent node supports conversational memory, tools, and sub-workflows.

---

name: LM Studio
desc: Cross-platform desktop application for discovering, downloading, and running quantized LLMs (GGUF format) completely offline on macOS, Windows, and Linux, exposing a local OpenAI-compatible REST server.
notes:
Free for personal use; commercial deployment requires LM Studio for Work license. Connects directly to Hugging Face to search and pull quantized model weights with automatic hardware GPU offloading.

---

name: LocalAI
desc: Free, open-source drop-in replacement REST API compatible with OpenAI specifications for local and edge inference. Runs text generation, vision, audio transcription, image generation, and embeddings without requiring cloud connectivity.
notes:
MIT-licensed. Built by Ettore Di Giacinto (mudler). Supports multiple backends including llama.cpp, Whisper.cpp, Diffusers, and ONNX inside standard Docker containers on consumer CPUs and GPUs.

name: Jan
subtype: Open-Source Offline Local AI Desktop Client
desc: 100% open-source, privacy-first desktop application and local API server that runs LLMs locally on personal hardware. Stores all conversations, models, and embeddings locally on disk without telemetry tracking.
notes:
AGPL-3.0 licensed. Developed by Menhir. Powered by the Nitro inference engine (C++). Exposes a local HTTP server at `http://localhost:1337` mimicking OpenAI chat endpoints for local development.

name: MLX

desc: Efficient machine learning framework designed specifically for Apple Silicon by Apple machine learning research. Features unified memory architecture exploitation, multi-device array operations, and lazy evaluation for fast local inference.

MIT-licensed. Uses Python and C++ APIs designed intentionally similar to NumPy and PyTorch. Powers `mlx-lm` for running high-parameter LLMs locally with high throughput on M1/M2/M3/M4 MacBooks.

name: DeepEval
subtype: Unit Testing & Evaluation Framework for LLM Apps
desc: Open-source evaluation and unit testing framework for LLM applications. Provides production-grade metrics for evaluating hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, G-Eval, and prompt injection defense within CI/CD pipelines.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Designed to integrate directly with `pytest` for automated regression testing of prompt updates, model swaps, and retrieval adjustments. Confident AI provides cloud tracking dashboards.

desc: Open-source framework tailored for evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. Computes reference-free scores for context precision, context recall, faithfulness, and answer relevance to pinpoint retrieval versus generation failures.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by Exploding Gradients. Features synthetic test dataset generation capabilities using document corpuses to automate comprehensive RAG benchmark suites.
